Definition: from χαράσσω (to sharpen to a point; akin to G1125 through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege):--trench.
BiblicalUsage: Charax is a palisade, a trench, a sharpened stake, and it appears once, in Jesus' weeping over Jerusalem: thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the single verse is a prophecy with a date on it: the trench Jesus described is the one Rome would dig.
